metadata.description: AArch64 (ubuntu-24.04-arm) regression baseline. baseline_value IS the measured median on the canonical runner (no pre-discounting); tolerance_percent is the single derived allowance. The runner fleet is homogeneous (cross-run spreads <= 3% for deterministic primitives over the 2026-08-14 calibration runs), so tolerance is 15, or 25 for the rejection-averaged composites dilithium_sign and full_package_create. The gate fires at a 15-25% regression; the previous 65%-floor-times-35-70%-tolerance convention compounded to a 34-94% blind spot and absorbed a 2.1x AES-GCM wrapper regression without firing. Updates require line-item justification per benchmarks/check_baseline_justification.py.
metadata.system: GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04-arm shared runner, Linux AArch64, Python 3.11
metadata.notes: Re-measured 2026-08-14 on the benchmark-regression job's ubuntu-24.04-arm runner across five CI runs of the repaired harness (sample-window sizing, fastest-of-three full-window batches, and input cycling for the deterministic-ML-DSA rejection-sampling benchmarks). aes_256_gcm_encrypt and chacha20poly1305_encrypt are floored from the final-wrapper-state runs only: the one-shot AEAD wrapper work in this same release moved their throughput (AES 132k -> ~234k ops/sec), so earlier runs measure a wrapper the tree no longer has — the exact staleness mode that let the May 2026 floors drift to 0.55x-9.54x of measured.

baseline_change_log.reason: Recalibrated to 65% of current measured performance (1,017 ops/sec measured on ubuntu-latest, see benchmark-results.json 2026-04-21T01:06:23Z). ML-DSA-65 signing is rejection-sampling based and its throughput on shared CI runners varies significantly with rejection rate for a fixed message; the v2.1.2 baseline of 1,918 ops/sec was measured on a less-loaded runner. No code regression: ML-DSA-65 keygen (2,951 ops/sec) and verify (6,322 ops/sec) both show -52% and -47% deltas (faster than baseline) on the same run, confirming the sign-side number is a runner-variance recalibration, not a C-level slowdown. 35% regression headroom preserved via the `tolerance_percent: 40` entry.

Re-floored after observing stable runner-variance on a slower contended sandbox host (3-run medians taken with build configured at -DAMA_ENABLE_AVX512=ON; AVX-512 SHA3 4-way kernel landed in this release). Each baseline set to ~65% of the slowest-runner stable median so even a contended GitHub-hosted shared runner clears the regression threshold without false positives; canonical Sapphire Rapids / Zen 4 hosts continue to clear by a wide negative-regression margin (faster than baseline). full_package_create tolerance bumped 50%→70% to absorb the GC-stall variance observed at 3-run min/max ratios > 2.5x. README, benchmark-report.md, and wiki/Performance-Benchmarks.md continue to publish the canonical-host throughput numbers — those are distinct from this regression floor, which is the worst-case-runner safety net. Source measurements: stable-medians captured 2026-04-25 across 30+ runs of validation_suite.py and 10+ runs of benchmark_runner.py; full_package_verify floor lowered 2044→700 to absorb the borderline 47–55% variance band. Source measurements: 3-run medians captured 2026-04-25, full transcript saved alongside benchmark-results.json on the consolidate branch.

Populated ARM baseline require infrastructure: replaced first-run zero placeholders with 65% regression floors from successful AArch64 benchmark measurements so CI fails on real ARM regressions instead of accepting unpopulated baselines.

baseline_change_log.change: WINDOW EXTENDED, FLOORS CARRIED FORWARD UNVERIFIED. The x86-64 baseline was re-floored for 3.4.0 against fresh measurements; these AArch64 floors were NOT, because recalibrating them requires the ubuntu-24.04-arm runner and no AArch64 hardware was available. No floor value in this file was changed, so the AArch64 gate is exactly as strong as it was before — but it is still calibrated against v2.1.2 and therefore still far looser than it should be. ACTION REQUIRED: re-measure on the benchmark-regression job's ubuntu-24.04-arm matrix entry and re-floor at 0.65 * measured, matching what benchmarks/baseline.json now does for x86-64. Recorded here rather than left implicit so the carry-forward is auditable.

WINDOW EXTENDED, FLOORS CARRIED FORWARD UNCHANGED. The tree-delta argument for extending the window to 3.5.0 is the same as for the x86-64 file — PR #380, the only change since 66d2073, touches no src/c kernel, dispatch path, or Python hot path — but unlike the x86-64 file these floors were NOT re-measured on 2026-07-29: they remain the 2026-05-15 ubuntu-24.04-arm calibration (PR #305; secp256k1 rows added by PR #370), carried forward exactly as the 2026-07-29 entry records, and that entry's ACTION REQUIRED to re-measure on the ubuntu-24.04-arm matrix runner still stands. No floor value in this file was re-measured or altered.

PROVENANCE METADATA CORRECTED, NO FLOOR CHANGES. `baseline_source_release` said 2.1.2 and `notes` was an x86-64 copy-paste (‘Sapphire Rapids / Zen 4 hosts’, a 2026-04-25 recalibration this file never had); no floor in this file ever came from a v2.1.2 measurement — they date from the 2026-05-15 PR #305 ARM run (secp256k1 rows: PR #370). `baseline_source_release` now names 3.1.0, the release current at that measurement, and `notes` now describes this file. This also corrects the 2026-07-29 entry's ‘still calibrated against v2.1.2’ aside — historical entries are records and were left verbatim; the correction lives here.

WINDOW EXTENDED TO 4.0.0, NO FLOOR CHANGES. The 4.0.0 major bump pushed the package past `applies_through_release` (3.5.0) and tripped test_benchmark_baseline_freshness. Every `baseline_value` in this file is carried forward unchanged; only `applies_through_release` moved. Rationale: of the primitives this file floors, 4.0.0 touches exactly one measured path — Ed25519 verify and point decode gain `ama_ed25519_point_y_is_canonical`, a single branch-free 32-byte comparison per decode, against a verify costing ~10^5 ns. The scalar-GHASH rewrite earlier in this release affects only the non-SIMD AES-GCM fallback; the AArch64 runner class named in `system` dispatches `aes_256_gcm_encrypt` to the PMULL/NEON kernel, so it measures the same code as before. No other floored primitive changed — ed25519_keygen, ed25519_sign, ed25519_verify, secp256k1_ecdsa_sign, secp256k1_ecdsa_verify, ama_sha3_256_hash, hmac_sha3_256, hkdf_derive, dilithium_keygen, dilithium_sign, dilithium_verify, kyber_keygen, kyber_encapsulate, aes_256_gcm_encrypt, chacha20poly1305_encrypt, x25519_scalarmult, full_package_create and full_package_verify all keep their existing floors. AUTHORITY: these floors were NOT re-measured for this entry, and no AArch64 measurement of any kind was taken for it. The canonical measurement is the benchmark-regression (aarch64) CI job, which runs on the calibrated runner class named in `system` and gates this PR. The sandbox numbers recorded in the sibling x86-64 `baseline.json` entry for this release were measured on an x86-64 host and bear on that file only: this file's Ed25519 floors are 11855/30266/28626 ops/sec for verify/sign/keygen, not the x86-64 file's 13000/33000/31000, and no cross-architecture comparison between the two is meaningful. (Corrected 2026-08-01: as first written, this entry quoted the x86-64 floors and that x86-64 sandbox run as though they bore on this file — the same x86-64 copy-paste into the AArch64 baseline that the 2026-07-30 entry above exists to correct.) If the aarch64 benchmark-regression job fails on this PR, these floors need a genuine canonical re-measure, not a further window extension.

KEYGEN FLOORS RE-MEASURED FOR INVARIANT-41 (PR #391): key generation now includes the FIPS 140-3 pairwise consistency test on every keypair — a sign+verify for signature keys, an encapsulate+decapsulate for KEM keys — so the keygen benchmarks measure keygen-plus-PCT, deliberately: hiding the test from the benchmark would report a cost users do not get. Floors are set to the canonical benchmark-regression CI job's measurements on the PCT-bearing head (commit f195e69): ed25519_keygen 28626 -> 10116 ops/sec, dilithium_keygen 2700 -> 1705 ops/sec, kyber_keygen 4094 -> 3684 ops/sec. Only ed25519_keygen, dilithium_keygen and kyber_keygen change; no other primitive's measured path was touched by INVARIANT-41 (x25519_scalarmult and the secp256k1/sign/verify/encrypt benches do not generate keys). AUTHORITY: these ARE the canonical runner's own measurements, taken from the failing gate run itself on ubuntu-24.04-arm (AArch64).

FULL RECALIBRATION FROM THE REPAIRED HARNESS (PR #394). baseline_value becomes the measured median (slow-class median for x86) and tolerance_percent the single derived allowance — see description. Every primitive changed; per-primitive from/to values with measurements and runner identifiers are in the recalibration commit message and in calibration_evidence.per_primitive. baseline_source_release advances to 4.0.0, making the freshness window honest for the first time since 2026-05-15 (ARM) / 2026-07-29 (x86).

WINDOW EXTENDED TO 5.0.0, NO FLOOR CHANGES. The 5.0.0 major bump pushes the package past `applies_through_release` (4.0.0) and would trip test_benchmark_baseline_freshness. Every `baseline_value` in this file is carried forward unchanged; only `applies_through_release` moves. Rationale: these floors ARE the 2026-08-14 full recalibration recorded in the previous entry — measured in this same PR (#394) from the repaired harness on the canonical benchmark-regression runner class for this file (ubuntu-24.04-arm, AArch64) — and 5.0.0 is cut from the tree those medians describe. The only commits between the recalibration head and the 5.0.0 cut are: the CodeQL alert cleanup (an error-path log line in `keypair_generate`'s ctypes guard, import-style unification), the fail-closed unreadable-candidate rule in library discovery (load-time, not per-operation), the binding-extension digest signing (build- and import-time), CI probe and C-test-lane fixes, documentation and CHANGELOG restructuring, and the version bump itself. No src/c kernel, no dispatch path, and no Python hot-path wrapper changed after the floors were measured, so the floors describe exactly the code 5.0.0 ships — the same tree-delta argument as the 3.5.0 and 4.0.0 window extensions above, this time with floors measured inside the same PR rather than carried forward from an earlier release. AUTHORITY: no new measurement was taken for this entry; the benchmark-regression (aarch64) CI job gates this PR against these floors on the canonical runner class, which is the check that matters. If that job fails on this PR, the floors need a genuine canonical re-measure, not a further window extension.

calibration_evidence.harness: benchmarks/benchmark_runner.py with sample-window sizing, fastest-of-three full-window batches, and 256-input cycling for the rejection-sampled benchmarks

ama_sha3_256_hash.description: AMA native C SHA3-256 hashing of 1KB data (FIPS 202, ctypes)

ed25519_sign.description: Ed25519 signature generation (native C, expanded key)

secp256k1_ecdsa_sign.description: secp256k1 ECDSA signing (native C, RFC 6979 deterministic nonce)

secp256k1_ecdsa_verify.description: secp256k1 ECDSA verification (native C, Shamir's-trick joint multiply, low-s + canonical-pubkey policy)

x25519_scalarmult.description: X25519 single-shot Diffie-Hellman scalar-mult (native C, default dispatch). Backed by fe64 (radix-2^64, MULX/ADX) on x86-64 hosts with BMI2+ADX, fe51 (radix-2^51) on 64-bit hosts without, and gf16 on 32-bit. The AVX2 4-way kernel is OPT-IN via AMA_DISPATCH_USE_X25519_AVX2=1 and is intentionally not faster than scalar fe64 on MULX/ADX hosts — see src/c/dispatch/ama_dispatch.c:478-502 and tests/test_x25519_dispatch_policy.py for the dispatch contract. Re-floored 5,000 → 13,000 (2026-04-27 audit) so the regression gate actually catches a >40% drop from canonical-host throughput rather than ignoring it.

x25519_scalarmult_batch4.description: X25519 batch-4 Diffie-Hellman under default dispatch — measures BATCHES/SEC, not per-op rate. On MULX/ADX hosts this is roughly x25519_scalarmult / 4 plus the wrapper's per-batch overhead (canonical-host run measured ~4,100 batches/sec vs ~17,000 single-shot ops/sec). A significantly slower batches/sec number typically means the AVX2 4-way kernel was accidentally selected as the default — that is a regression on every shipped Broadwell+/Zen+ part (see PR #273 design note and ama_dispatch.c:478-502). The runner calls native_x25519_scalarmult_batch with count=4 so this baseline genuinely exercises the batch wrapper, not four sequential native_x25519_key_exchange calls.
